items.title: [Bug]: `/metrics` (iteration-stats) route blocks the serve event loop — a 2 s Prometheus scrape inflates request latency 5–60× and cuts prefill throughput ~5× (4× RTX 5060 Ti TP4, Qwen3.5 hybrid-GDN NVFP4 27B, 1.3.0rc29)
items.author: sean640112
items.body_excerpt:
> **Update (2026-10-09): the root cause is not sm120.** The "fixed" per-request cost comes from the `/metrics` iteration-stats route blocking the serve event loop: a 2 s Prometheus scrape inflates request latency 5–60× and cuts prefill throughput ~5×. Controlled A/B, py-spy stacks and the Prometheus-side numbers are in the [follow-up comment](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/19623#issuecomment-6076428189) below.

# ~6 s fixed per-request latency floor on sm120 (4× RTX 5060 Ti, TP4) with a Qwen3.5 hybrid-GDN 27B NVFP4 checkpoint

## Summary

On a 4× RTX 5060 Ti (sm120) box serving a **dense hybrid GDN + full-attention 27B** NVFP4 checkpoint with `trtllm-serve` (PyTorch backend, TP4), we measure a **~6 s per-request floor on time-to-first-token that is independent of prompt length**. A 212-token request takes **6.06 s** to first token (8.0 s total), and the floor persists at every length we tested (212 → 59,571 tokens). Requests are reproducible to ±5 ms across 12 measurements in 3 separate server starts.

The same hardware, same checkpoint, same prompt, same client, served by SGLang gives **0.26–0.30 s** for the identical request. `trtllm-serve` therefore looks ~20× slower on short requests, while its *marginal* prefill throughput is only ~2.6× lower (~2,143 tok/s vs ~5,600 tok/s).

We have ruled out MTP/spec-decode, scheduler policy, `max_seq_len`, chunked prefill, the CUDA caching allocator, and thinking-mode as causes (details below). We would like to know whether this per-request floor is **expected on sm120 for hybrid GDN models**, or a bug — and which knob/diagnostic we should look at next. We are happy to run any instrumentation you suggest.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 4× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, compute capability **12.0 (sm120)**, TP=4 |
| Driver | 610.57.04 |
| CUDA toolkit | 13.3 (`nvcc` 13.3, `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3`) |
| OS / Python | Linux, Python 3.12.11 (venv) |
| TensorRT-LLM | **1.3.0rc29.dev202609240000** (nightly from 2026-09-24; PyPI 1.2.1 does not contain `modeling_qwen3_5.py`, hence nightly) |
| torch | 2.14.0+cu132 |
| flashinfer-python | 0.6.18 |
| triton | 3.8.0 |
| nvidia-cutlass-dsl | 4.8.0.dev0 |
| tensorrt / tensorrt_cu13 | 10.14.1.48.post1 |
| MPI | OpenMPI 5.0.10 (`mpi4py` bootstrap path) |
| Model | `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` — `architectures: ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"]`, `model_type: qwen3_5`; 64 layers, hidden 5120, 24 Q heads, 4 KV heads |
| Quantization | ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION`: **FP8 per-tensor on 208 layers** (`block_size` absent) + **NVFP4 `group_size: 16` on 193 layers**, `kv_cache_quant_algo: null` |

Note on the attention backend: your hardware support matrix lists sm120 as supporting NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 (per-tensor) / FP8 KV cache, which covers this checkpoint's formats — so the quantization scheme itself should be fully supported on sm120.

## How to reproduce

Server (the `mpirun -n 1` wrapper and `OMPI_MCA_*` are needed on this host because `import tensorrt_llm` otherwise blocks in the mpi4py `MPI.COMM_WORLD` initialization, and this host's own hostname resolves to loopback only):

```bash
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3
export OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=lo OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=lo
mpirun -n 1 --oversubscribe trtllm-serve serve /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 1234 --tp_size 4 \
  --max_seq_len 140000 --max_batch_size 8 \
  --served_model_name qwen3.8-27b \
  --free_gpu_memory_fraction 0.80 \
  --extra_llm_api_options opts.yaml
```

`opts.yaml`:
```yaml
enable_chunked_prefill: true
max_num_tokens: 8192
speculative_config:
  decoding_type: MTP
  max_draft_len: 3
  speculative_model: /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4
```

Client — a minimal stdlib-only streaming client (this is the "probe" used for every number below; it measures the first chunk that carries `choices[0].text`/`delta.content`):

```python
import json, time, urllib.request
prompt = open("/path/to/corpus.txt").read()[:600]          # → 212 tokens
body = {"model": "qwen3.8-27b", "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "stream": True}
req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/completions",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
t0 = time.time(); ttft = None
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900) as r:
    for raw in r:
        s = raw.decode().strip()
        if not s.startswith("data: "): continue
        if s[6:] == "[DONE]": break
        d = json.loads(s[6:])
        ch = d.get("choices") or []
        if ch and ch[0].get("text"):
            ttft = time.time() - t0; break
print("TTFT", ttft)
```

## Measured results (same probe, same prompts, same box)

| prompt tokens | path | TRT-LLM stream TTFT | TRT-LLM non-stream total | SGLang stream TTFT | SGLang non-stream total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **212** | completions | **6.053–6.062 s** (n=5) | 7.995–8.035 s | **0.262 s** | 0.304 s |
| 222 | chat (medium template) | 12.11 – **22.21 s** (unstable across restarts) | 14.06 – 26.19 s | 0.268 s | — |
| 7,172 | completions | 10.10 s | 12.02 s | 0.243 s *cached* | 1.84 s *cached* |
| 12,131 | completions | 12.12 s | 14.06 s | — | — |
| 28,008 | completions | — | 20.13 s | — | 6.15 s *cached* |
| 59,571 | completions | — | 36.26 s | — | — |
| 65,032 | chat | 56.52 s | 56.45 s | — | — |

*("cached" = the SGLang side hit its radix prefix cache on the shared corpus prefix, so those cells are not a like-for-like prefill comparison.)*

Least-squares fit of the completions path (`total = C + N/R`, 5 points spanning 212 → 59,571 tokens):
**C = 8.10 s, R = 2,143 tok/s, R² = 0.9966** — i.e. a very large constant plus a modest rate term. (The streaming TTFT is ≈ 1.9 s lower at every point, i.e. TTFT ≈ 6.1 s + N/2143.)

For reference, an independent client (vLLM's `bench serve` against the same server) measured prefill throughput of **453 / 1,014 / 1,302 tok/s** at 8K / 32K / 64K with meanTTFT 16.15 / 29.28 / 46.44 s, i.e. the same

items.title: [Bug] FP8 ragged prefill refcheck mismatch between trtllm-native and prims-ts on B200/GB300
items.author: yufeiwu-nv
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

The official BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper benchmark reports an FP8 output mismatch between trtllm-native and prims-ts on B200 and GB300. Both backends execute for this supported configuration, but their outputs fail the benchmark's current torch.isclose check (rtol=0.2, atol=0.01).

This reports a reproducible benchmark/backend-consistency failure. It does not establish which implementation is wrong or identify an introducing commit.

## Environment and supported configuration

- FlashInfer version printed by the benchmark: 0.7.2.
- Latest observed reproducing revisions: B200 f63b2e7; GB300 5f8c9ef. Their ragged benchmark source is byte-identical.
- Q/K/V: FP8 E4M3; output: BF16; causal dense ragged prefill.
- Q and KV heads: 16; QK head dimension: 192; V/output head dimension: 128.
- Batch sizes 1 and 4, each with Q/KV sequence length 2048 or 4096; seed 42; default CUDA-graph setting.
- deepseek-v4-pro_861b is a benchmark case label. These commands exercise synthetic dense attention, not an end-to-end model or sparse-MLA validation.

## Reproduction

From the public repository's benchmarks/ directory at an observed revision, with that revision's benchmark dependencies installed, run these exact commands on B200 or GB300:

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper --backends trtllm-native prims-ts --batch_size 1 --s_qo 2048 --s_kv 2048 --num_qo_heads 16 --num_kv_heads 16 --head_dim_qk 192 --head_dim_vo 128 --causal --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --out_dtype bfloat16 --refcheck --allow_output_mismatch --random_seed 42 -vv --generate_repro_command --case_tag deepseek-v4-pro_861b
```

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper --backends trtllm-native prims-ts --batch_size 1 --s_qo 4096 --s_kv 4096 --num_qo_heads 16 --num_kv_heads 16 --head_dim_qk 192 --head_dim_vo 128 --causal --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --out_dtype bfloat16 --refcheck --allow_output_mismatch --random_seed 42 -vv --generate_repro_command --case_tag deepseek-v4-pro_861b
```

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper --backends trtllm-native prims-ts --batch_size 4 --s_qo 2048 --s_kv 2048 --num_qo_heads 16 --num_kv_heads 16 --head_dim_qk 192 --head_dim_vo 128 --causal --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --out_dtype bfloat16 --refcheck --allow_output_mismatch --random_seed 42 -vv --generate_repro_command --case_tag deepseek-v4-pro_861b
```

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper --backends trtllm-native prims-ts --batch_size 4 --s_qo 4096 --s_kv 4096 --num_qo_heads 16 --num_kv_heads 16 --head_dim_qk 192 --head_dim_vo 128 --causal --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --out_dtype bfloat16 --refcheck --allow_output_mismatch --random_seed 42 -vv --generate_repro_command --case_tag deepseek-v4-pro_861b
```

The commands retain the original --allow_output_mismatch setting, so a mismatch does not stop timing. Without that option, the source raises on a mismatch; that modified command has not been rerun separately.

## Observed result

For batch size 1 and sequence length 2048 at the latest observed revisions:

```text
B200:
[ERROR] Output tensor mismatch between backends trtllm-native and prims-ts: 2211 / 4194304 (0.05%) elements are different

GB300:
[ERROR] Output tensor mismatch between backends trtllm-native and prims-ts: 2205 / 4194304 (0.05%) elements are different
```

The same primary signature appears for all four shapes on both GPUs: 88 completed benchmark executions across six B200 revisions and five GB300 revisions, with two repetitions for each shape/revision. These executions come from one CI pipeline; no independent paired rerun or causal bisect is claimed.

Immediately before every mismatch, prims-ts passes its eight sampled FP32 context-reference checks and CUDA-graph replay-reference checks. Those checks support investigation but do not establish complete-tensor ground truth or prove that trtllm-native is incorrect.

## Source attribution and expected behavior

Both backend configurations are accepted by the upstream benchmark's support checks. The dense ragged routine sets rtol=2e-1 and atol=1e-2 and calls is_close_stats, which uses torch.isclose elementwise. The counts represent values beyond that declared tolerance, rather than a request for bitwise agreement.

When FA2 is unavailable, the routine uses trtllm-native as its inter-backend comparison reference while independently checking sampled prims-ts outputs against FP32 attention. Reference priority alone does not establish implementation correctness.

Please investigate the backend discrepancy or the benchmark's FP8 comparison/reference contract. Supported backend results should satisfy the benchmark's declared validation criterion, or the benchmark should explain and validate a justified alternative criterion.

- [Ragged benchmark source](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/f63b2e7/benchmarks/routines/attention.py#L2397)
- [Elementwise comparison helper](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/f63b2e7/benchmarks/routines/flashinfer_benchmark_utils.py#L385)
- [B200 completed CI evidence](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/483764444)
- [GB300 completed CI evidence](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/483764439)

items.title: Should LMCacheMPConnector honor kv_transfer_config.kv_role — or is MP mode intentionally always-kv_both?
items.author: kezboard233
items.body_excerpt:
## Context

We run a production-shaped POC on 8×V100 (two vLLM TP4 instances of Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 sharing one LMCache MP server with a CPU L1 tier) and filed #5143 with a runtime-verified repro: an engine launched with `kv_role="kv_consumer"` still stores every request's KV into the shared L1 — a single 32K-token cold request produced `168 × "Stored 784"` lines (= full prefix × 4 TP ranks), and the only engine that received any request in that window was the `kv_consumer` one.

We later found #4665 (closed by its author without maintainer response) reporting the same mechanism from the CacheBlend angle: the single-process connector honors `kv_role` / `skip_save`, the MP connector honors neither. As of today's `dev`, `lmcache_mp_connector.py` still contains no occurrence of `kv_role` / `kv_consumer` / `kv_producer` / `force_skip_save`.

## The design question

Before we contribute a patch, we want to check intent: **is MP mode intentionally "every connected engine writes"?** Two readings:

1. **Contract gap** — vLLM makes `kv_role` mandatory, documents it as "Whether this vLLM instance produces, consumes KV cache, or both", and exposes `is_kv_producer` / `is_kv_consumer` for connectors to branch on; LMCache's own single-process adapter honors it (`force_skip_save` in `vllm_v1_adapter.py`). Under this reading we'd gladly contribute a small PR that skips store-metadata generation when `is_kv_consumer` (mirroring the single-process gate), so warm-then-read-only fleets and PD-style topologies become possible on the MP path.

2. **Intentional always-kv_both** — the MP tier is a shared scratch space where every connected engine contributes. Under this reading we'd instead ask for the intent to be documented, plus ideally a one-line warning at connector init when `kv_role != "kv_both"`, so users aren't misled (we only noticed via instrumented counter evidence ourselves).

Happy to do either — a steer from maintainers decides which.

(Impact context: no correctness issue — stored content is identical — but a consumer-role engine burns D2H bandwidth and shared-L1 capacity; a 32K prefix on our model is ≈8.6 GB across 4 ranks.)

items.title: [Performance]: Beam search re-materializes Result.output_token_ids from pybind once per beam
items.author: yifanQi98
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

#### Background

For beam-search requests, `GenerationResultBase._handle_response` iterates over beams and calls `_handle_sequence` once per beam:

```python
finish_reasons = response_result.finish_reasons
# output_token_ids = (beams, tokens)
if self.sampling_params.use_beam_search:
    for beam_idx, _ in enumerate(response_result.output_token_ids):   # result.py:692
        self._handle_sequence(finish_reasons, response_result,
                              beam_idx, logprobs_result,
                              req_perf_metrics_dict)
```

`_handle_sequence` then reads the same property again, once per call:

```python
if self.sampling_params.use_beam_search:
    output.token_ids = [
        *decoder_output_prefix,
        *response_tensors.output_token_ids[src_idx],      # result.py:402
    ]
else:
    ...
    output.token_ids.extend(response_tensors.output_token_ids[src_idx])   # result.py:407
```

`LlmResult.output_token_ids` is not in `LlmResult.py_result_properties`, so `LlmResult.__getattr__` falls through to `getattr(self._result, item)` on the **pybind** `bindings.executor.Result`. That property returns a freshly built nested Python list on every access — it is not cached on either side:

```python
>>> a, b = llm_result.output_token_ids, llm_result.output_token_ids
>>> a is b
False
>>> a[0] is b[0]
False
>>> a == b
True
```

So for a request with `N` beams, one response converts the full `(N, tokens)` structure from C++ **N + 1 times** when once is sufficient. Because the per-conversion cost is itself O(N · tokens), the redundant work is **quadratic in beam width**.

This is the dominant host-side cost for the "short decode length, very wide beams" pattern (e.g. SID / generative-recommendation serving with `n = best_of = 500`, `max_tokens = 3`), where `_handle_sequence` does almost no work per beam other than these reads.

#### Measurement

Offline, no GPU, no model, no executor. A real `bindings.executor.Result` is constructed and populated (`output_token_ids` is settable), wrapped in a real `LlmResult`, and the **real** `GenerationResultBase._handle_sequence` is driven once per beam, reproducing the body of `_handle_response`'s beam loop. (Correction added after review: this driver loop used `range(BEAM)` and so did not include the loop head's own `enumerate(response_result.output_token_ids)` read. It therefore measures N reads per response rather than the N+1 a real response performs; at 500 beams that is one extra ~26 us read, about 0.2% of the effect.)

Three arms, interleaved, `gc.collect()` before every sample, median of 25:

- **A stock** — real `_handle_sequence` against the real `LlmResult`
- **C patched** — the same real source, textually rewritten so `response_tensors.output_token_ids` resolves to a binding materialized **once per response**; every other attribute still reads the real `LlmResult` per beam, so this arm does not overstate the win. (Correction added after review: the rewrite binds the value through a module-level global to model the hoist. It is semantically the suggested fix but is not literally the final parameter-passing form; the re-measurement below uses the real patch.)
- **B snapshot** — every attribute pre-materialized, with the snapshot itself built outside the timed region. It bounds the achievable *saving*; it is **not** a measurement of what any real memoizing implementation would cost, since that implementation has to build and consult its cache inside the timed region

Access counts were obtained by running the real code path against a counting forwarder, not by reading the source by hand. For one 500-beam response:

| attribute | reads | served by |
|---|---|---|
| `time_breakdown_metrics` | 1000 | instance attr (cheap) |
| `output_token_ids` | **500** | **pybind** |
| `request_perf_metrics` | **500** | **pybind** |
| `cum_log_probs` / `log_probs` / `generation_logits` / `additional_*_outputs` | 500 each | `py_result` (Python-side) |
| `finish_reasons` | 1 | pybind |

Total 4501 attribute reads per response, 1001 of them pybind-served.

##### Results (ms per response, `tokens = 3`)

| beams | one pybind read | A stock | C patched | C saving | B upper bound | B saving |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.53 µs | 0.122 | 0.120 | −0.002 (1.6%) | 0.097 | −0.025 (20.5%) |
| 20 | 1.25 µs | 0.195 | 0.187 | −0.008 (4.1%) | 0.127 | −0.068 (34.9%) |
| 100 | 6.25 µs | 1.016 | 0.458 | −0.558 (54.9%) | 0.303 | −0.713 (70.2%) |
| 300 | 16.20 µs | 5.848 | 1.047 | −4.801 (82.1%) | 0.682 | −5.166 (88.3%) |
| **500** | **25.94 µs** | **14.428** | **1.543** | **−12.885 (89.3%)** | 0.985 | −13.443 (93.2%) |

At 500 beams, **89% of the per-response beam loop is redundant pybind re-conversion of one property.** 100 → 500 beams is 5× the width and 23× the waste, confirming the quadratic behaviour.

In this harness the effect at beam=20 is inside its noise floor (arm C's delta is 0.008 ms against a per-sample sd of 0.03–0.04 ms). That is a limit of this harness's precision, **not** a general threshold: the re-measurement below, using the real patch and 60 interleaved pairs, resolves a repeatable 0.025–0.028 ms saving at 20 beams with a 95% CI of [0.0250, 0.0306]. The saving is simply small there, and it grows quadratically.

##### Cross-check

Two independent estimates of the same quantity agree:

- micro: 500 reads × 25.94 µs = **12.97 ms**
- macro: arm A − arm C = **12.89 ms**
- ratio **0.99**

The residual between arm C and arm B (0.558 ms at 500 beams) is **not** mostly `request_perf_metrics`. Corrected attribution, measured directly rather than inferred from the residual: a per-read micro-benchmark puts `request_perf_metrics` at **0.241 µs** unset / **0.361 µs** set, so its 499 per-beam reads are worth **0.120 ms** (unset) / **0.180 ms** (set) per response, and hoisting it in situ measures 0.165 ms. The larger share of the residual is the per-beam group served Python-side by `PyResult` (`log_probs`, `cum_log_probs`,

items.title: [Bug]: trtllm-serve /v1/chat/completions rejects the standard OpenAI field prompt_cache_key with 400
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

TensorRT-LLM main @ 15f060c9f8, `trtllm-serve` (any model, any GPU).

### Reproduction

    curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
      "model": "<model>",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
      "prompt_cache_key": "session-1234"
    }'

or with the OpenAI Python client: `client.chat.completions.create(..., prompt_cache_key="session-1234")`.

### Expected behavior

The request is served. `prompt_cache_key` is part of OpenAI's Chat Completions request body (a hint for prompt-cache routing), and clients built on it may set it on every request of a session.

### Actual behavior

The request fails validation with `extra_forbidden` ("Extra inputs are not permitted") for `prompt_cache_key`, because `ChatCompletionRequest` inherits `extra="forbid"` from `OpenAIBaseModel` and has no such field. `ResponsesRequest` already accepts it (it switched to `extra="allow"`, and the comment there names `prompt_cache_key` as one of the fields real clients send), so the same client works against `/v1/responses` but not against `/v1/chat/completions`.

### Additional notes

KV cache reuse in TensorRT-LLM needs no client hint, and `cache_salt` is the field that isolates cached prefixes, so the field can be accepted and ignored, the same way `parallel_tool_calls` and `user` are. PR to follow.

items.title: [Bug]: Grouped MLA generation cubins are registered as Dense in kernelMetaInfo.h but named and selected as Causal
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

TensorRT-LLM main, `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/trtllmGenKernels/fmha/cubin/kernelMetaInfo.h` (artifacts from #19591). Seen on SM107; the SM100f rows have the same pattern.

### Who can help?

@pengbowang-nv @farazkh80 (#15009)

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

All 36 grouped MLA generation cubins in `kernelMetaInfo.h` (`fmhaSm100fKernel_...` and `fmhaSm107aKernel_QkvBfloat16OBfloat16HQk576HV512{,HVPerCta128,HVPerCta256}PagedKvCausalP32...VarSeqQ64Kv128{Static,Persistent}GroupedKeepsAbForGen`, 18 for `kSM_100f`, 18 for `kSM_107`) have `Causal` in the function name, but their `mMaskType` field is `0` (`TrtllmGenAttentionMaskType::Dense`).

`mMaskType` is part of the hash that the cubin path looks up (`hashFromFmhaOptions` -> `hashID`). With `FmhaOptions::mSelectsGroupedMla = true`, the autotuner selects the grouped kernel with a causal mask for MLA generation with multiple query tokens, so the lookup fails (`Trtllm-gen kernels not found`), and the only remaining route is NVRTC. On SM107, NVRTC currently fails for these configurations (separate issue). We had to map Causal back to Dense for grouped MLA kernels in `algoFilterForCubinPath` before the cubins could be used.

With that mapping, the cubins give the expected causal result: compared with the non-grouped kernel on SM107, outputs are bit-identical for KV lengths 16 and 64, and at most 2 bf16 ulp apart from 256 up to 128K. So the kernels behave as their names say, and only the metadata is off. #15009 also mentions that its re-exported rows were changed to `maskType=Causal` "to match the shipped lib's grouped mask rewrite".

### Expected behavior

The registered mask type matches what the kernel implements and what the selector asks for, so that grouped MLA generation cubins can be found without a remapping.

### actual behavior

`mMaskType = Dense` for kernels named `...Causal...`; the cubin lookup misses them when grouped MLA selection is enabled.

### additional notes

This does not affect main today because `mSelectsGroupedMla` is never set in TensorRT-LLM. It blocks enabling it (#15009), together with the missing `cumSeqLensQ/Kv` in the MLA generation path (#20375). If the right fix is on the export side, a regenerated `kernelMetaInfo.h` would be enough; otherwise I can send the remapping as a small PR.

Related: #20375, #20377, #20382 (FP8-KV grouped MLA hang for head counts that do not divide 64).

items.title: [Bug]: FP8-KV MLA generation hangs on SM107 with the grouped trtllm-gen E4M3 kernels when heads per rank do not divide 64 (e.g. 12)
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- GPU: SM107, 8 GPUs over 2 nodes (TP8 attention)
- TensorRT-LLM main @ 69a455ae974bcf9582c9a2cc4f7fd9a5f75680fe (code and cubin list checked there), PyTorch backend, TRTLLM attention backend
- Model: MLA model with 96 query heads -> 12 heads per rank at TP8 (kv_lora_rank 512, qk_rope_head_dim 64)
- kv_cache_config.dtype: fp8, tokens_per_block 32, MTP speculative decoding with 8 query tokens per step
- Grouped (tokens x heads in one Q tile) MLA generation kernel selection enabled locally (`FmhaOptions::mSelectsGroupedMla`; main does not set it, see #15009)

### Who can help?

@pengbowang-nv @farazkh80

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

1. Serve the model with `kv_cache_config.dtype: fp8` and grouped MLA generation selection enabled.
2. Startup never finishes: every rank stops in the first generation-shape attention call of the warmup (num_tokens=8, num_gen_requests=1, KV length 8). GPU utilization stays at 100 %, nothing is logged after `Attention workspace size is not enough, increase the size from 0 bytes to ...`. `TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL=0` does not change it.
3. A host-side backtrace of a rank shows the main thread inside the next cuBLAS call (`cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx -> cuKernelSetAttribute`), i.e. queued behind a kernel that never completes.
4. With synchronizing checkpoints in `MLA.forward_absorption_generation`: the q_nope bmm and `mla_rope_generation` (FP8 Q quantization, FP8 KV append, bmm scales) complete; the attention op does not. A sync right after the FMHA launch in `TllmGenFmhaRunner::run` never returns. The selected cubin is `fmhaSm107aKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16HQk576HV512HVPerCta256PagedKvCausalP32VarSeqQ64Kv128StaticGroupedKeepsAbForGen` (grid 2x2x1, numHeadsQ 12, maxSeqLenQ 8, multiCtasKv off for this KV length).

Standalone reproduction with the FMHA runner only (no model): `TllmGenFmhaRunner(E4M3, E4M3, E4M3, BF16)`, paged KV page 32, MLA head dims 576/512, 1 KV head, generation kernel, grouped selection enabled, seqLenQ 8 (12 heads also hangs at seqLenQ 1, 4, 5, 6), seqLenKv 2048:

| numHeadsQ | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 20 | 24 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 (E4M3 Q/KV) grouped | ok | **hangs** | ok | **hangs** | **hangs** | **hangs** | ok | **hangs** | **hangs** | ok |
| BF16 grouped (checked: 12, 16) | — | — | — | — | ok | — | ok | — | — | — |

The FP8 kernel completes only when numHeadsQ divides the 64-row Q tile. BF16 grouped kernels with 12 heads are fine.

### Expected behavior

The FP8 grouped MLA generation kernel works for any head count, or is not selected for head counts it cannot handle.

### actual behavior

The FMHA kernel never completes; the process hangs with the GPU at 100 %.

### additional notes

**Analysis.** In `makeTmaShapeStrideQ` (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/trtllmGenKernels/fmha/trtllmGen_fmha_export/KernelParams.h`), for `mGroupsTokensHeadsQ`:

~~~
numTokensPerTileQ = numTokensPerTileQ / numGroupedHeads;   // 64 / 12 = 5
tileShapes = {clampedHeadDimQ, numGroupedHeads, 1, numTokensPerTileQ};  // 5 tokens x 12 heads = 60 rows
~~~

so the Q TMA box covers 60 of the 64 tile rows. The comment there says padding at the end of the tile is allowed. The BF16 cubins handle it; the E4M3 cubins never finish, which looks like the kernel waits for a full 64-row tile (a transaction byte count or row bookkeeping derived from tileSizeQ instead of from the box). Unchanged on current main.

**Reachability on main.** Main never sets `mSelectsGroupedMla`, so this hang is latent there today. But the precompiled SM107 E4M3 MLA generation cubins are KeepsAb only (Dense / Sliding / Sparse, plus the grouped ones above); there is no SwapsAb E4M3 MLA generation cubin. Non-grouped FP8 MLA generation on SM107 therefore goes to NVRTC and fails with `Array.cpp:376 Out-of-bound access` (#20377, case 2, including the 2048-query-token shape). I think the two are likely the same coverage gap seen from two sides: shapes without an E4M3 cubin fail in NVRTC, and the existing grouped E4M3 cubins hang when 64 % numHeadsQ != 0. The only FP8 MLA generation path that works on SM107 right now seems to be grouped selection with 4/8/16/32 heads per rank.

**Workaround** (removes the hang in our runs). In `AttentionOp::mlaGeneration` (TRTLLM-Gen path), when the selected kernel is grouped E4M3, Q is decode-size (<= 16 tokens) and `64 % numHeadsQ != 0`: copy Q into a zero-padded `[numTokens, nextPow2(numHeadsQ), 576]` FP8 buffer, run the FMHA with `mNumHeadsQ = mNumHeadsQPerKv = nextPow2(numHeadsQ)` and a padded BF16 output, then copy the real heads of O back (two small row-copy kernels; MLA heads are independent, so padded heads only produce output that is dropped). Not used when softmax stats, attention sinks or an output scale-factor buffer are requested. I have not opened a PR for it: it only matters once grouped selection is enabled (#15009, #20375, #20376), so it would be dead code on main as is; it could go in together with that change.

Possible proper fixes: (a) make the E4M3 grouped kernels handle a partial last tile like the BF16 ones; (b) build the Q TMA box from whole tokens rounded up, with OOB fill and row masking; (c) exclude such head counts from grouped selection for FP8 (on SM107 this currently lands on the NVRTC failure in #20377, so it needs that fixed too).

**End-to-end with the workaround** (one serving run, TP8 over 2 nodes, 8 query tokens per step, batch 1; the build also includes the split-KV reduction change from #20380; bf16 KV vs fp8 KV):

- Without the workaround: all ranks hang in the first generation warmup, as above. With it: startup completes, including CUDA graph capture for batch 16..1; no new errors in the logs.
- Decode step period (median, ms), bf16 KV -> fp8 KV: 2K 12.57 -> 12.64, 32K 12.87 -> 12.85, 128K 13.62 -> 13.39.
- Per MLA call (8 query tokens, 1 sequence): BF16 grouped with 12 heads vs FP8 grouped with 16 padded heads: 2K 12.16 v

items.title: trtllm-gen sparse MLA decode reads past a small KV cache (≤3 pages) → illegal memory access
items.author: MatthewBonanni
items.body_excerpt:
`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` in sparse mode (`sparse_mla_top_k=2048`, FP8 Q/KV, 64 heads, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, page size 64) reads past the end of the KV cache when the cache holds ≤3 pages (≤192 rows), even though every top-k index is in range. It only faults when the cache happens to end near an unmapped page, so in a server it shows up as a random illegal memory access depending on allocator placement.

**Environment:** flashinfer 0.7.0.post1, NVIDIA B200 (SM100), driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130.

Kernel: `fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16HQk576HV512PagedKvDenseStaticTokenSparseP1MultiCtasKvGmemSepVarSeqQ64Kv128StaticKeepsAbForGen` (compute-sanitizer: "Warp illegal address" at `+0x3530`; the error surfaces at the next launch, `runFmhaReduction`).

## Repro

The script maps one 2 MiB page with CUDA VMM (neighbouring pages reserved but unmapped) and places a `NUM_BLOCKS x 64`-row FP8 KV cache so it ends `SLACK_BYTES` before the end of that page. All top-k indices are `< NUM_BLOCKS * 64`; unused slots are `-1`.

<details><summary>sparse_mla_oob_repro.py</summary>

```python
"""trtllm-gen sparse MLA decode reads past the end of a small KV cache.

Places a KV cache of NUM_BLOCKS x 64 rows so that it ends exactly at the end of
a mapped 2 MiB page (the next page is reserved but unmapped), then runs sparse
MLA decode with in-range top-k indices.

usage: python sparse_mla_oob_repro.py NUM_BLOCKS [SLACK_BYTES]
"""

import ctypes
import sys

import torch
from flashinfer.decode import trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla

num_blocks = int(sys.argv[1])
slack = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0
block_size, num_heads, batch, top_k = 64, 64, 10, 2048
kv_lora_rank, qk_rope_head_dim, qk_nope_head_dim = 512, 64, 192
head_dim = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim
dev = torch.device("cuda")
fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
torch.manual_seed(0)

num_rows = num_blocks * block_size
seq_lens = torch.randint(1, num_rows + 1, (batch,), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
topk = torch.full((batch, top_k), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
for b, n in enumerate(seq_lens.tolist()):
    topk[b, :n] = torch.randperm(num_rows, device=dev)[:n].int()
q = (torch.randn(batch, 1, num_heads, head_dim, device=dev) * 0.1).to(fp8)
workspace = torch.zeros(128 << 20, dtype=torch.int8, device=dev)

# Reserve 3 x 2 MiB of VA and map only the middle page.
cu = ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1")


def check(rc, what):
    assert rc == 0, f"{what} failed: CUresult {rc}"


class AllocProp(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("type", ctypes.c_int),
        ("requestedHandleTypes", ctypes.c_int),
        ("loc_type", ctypes.c_int),
        ("loc_id", ctypes.c_int),
        ("win32HandleMetaData", ctypes.c_void_p),
        ("compressionType", ctypes.c_ubyte),
        ("gpuDirectRDMACapable", ctypes.c_ubyte),
        ("usage", ctypes.c_ushort),
        ("reserved", ctypes.c_ubyte * 4),
    ]


class AccessDesc(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("loc_type", ctypes.c_int), ("loc_id", ctypes.c_int), ("flags", ctypes.c_int)]


PAGE = 2 << 20
torch.cuda.synchronize()  # initialize the primary context
va = ctypes.c_uint64()
check(cu.cuMemAddressReserve(ctypes.byref(va), ctypes.c_size_t(3 * PAGE), ctypes.c_size_t(0), ctypes.c_uint64(0), ctypes.c_uint64(0)), "cuMemAddressReserve")
prop = AllocProp(type=1, loc_type=1, loc_id=torch.cuda.current_device())  # PINNED, DEVICE
handle = ctypes.c_uint64()
check(cu.cuMemCreate(ctypes.byref(handle), ctypes.c_size_t(PAGE), ctypes.byref(prop), ctypes.c_uint64(0)), "cuMemCreate")
page = va.value + PAGE
check(cu.cuMemMap(ctypes.c_uint64(page), ctypes.c_size_t(PAGE), ctypes.c_size_t(0), handle, ctypes.c_uint64(0)), "cuMemMap")
access = AccessDesc(loc_type=1, loc_id=prop.loc_id, flags=3)  # READWRITE
check(cu.cuMemSetAccess(ctypes.c_uint64(page), ctypes.c_size_t(PAGE), ctypes.byref(access), ctypes.c_size_t(1)), "cuMemSetAccess")

kv_bytes = num_rows * head_dim  # fp8: 1 byte per element
kv_ptr = page + PAGE - kv_bytes - slack


class _Buf:
    __cuda_array_interface__ = dict(shape=(kv_bytes,), typestr="|u1", data=(kv_ptr, False), version=3)


kv_cache = torch.as_tensor(_Buf(), device=dev).view(fp8).view(num_blocks, block_size, head_dim)
kv_cache.copy_((torch.randn(num_blocks, block_size, head_dim, device=dev) * 0.1).to(fp8))
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"num_blocks={num_blocks} rows={num_rows} kv_bytes={kv_bytes} slack={slack} max_index={int(topk.max())}", flush=True)

out = trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(
    query=q,
    kv_cache=kv_cache.unsqueeze(1),
    workspace_buffer=workspace,
    qk_nope_head_dim=qk_nope_head_dim,
    kv_lora_rank=kv_lora_rank,
    qk_rope_head_dim=qk_rope_head_dim,
    block_tables=topk.unsqueeze(1),
    seq_lens=seq_lens,
    max_seq_len=top_k,
    bmm1_scale=0.0625,
    bmm2_scale=1.0,
    sparse_mla_top_k=top_k,
)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print("ok", tuple(out.shape), flush=True)
```

</details>

```
$ for nb in 1 2 3 4 8; do python sparse_mla_oob_repro.py $nb; done
num_blocks=1 rows=64  ...  RuntimeError: Error in function 'runFmhaReduction' at csrc/fmhaReduction.cu:549: Failed to launch kernel:  an illegal memory access was encountered
num_blocks=2 rows=128 ...  (same)
num_blocks=3 rows=192 ...  (same)
num_blocks=4 rows=256 ...  ok (10, 1, 64, 512)
num_blocks=8 rows=512 ...  ok (10, 1, 64, 512)
```

**Expected:** the kernel reads only the KV rows named by the top-k indices (or at least stays within the KV cache tensor).
**Observed:** it reads well past the end of a small cache. Mapped slack needed after the cache before it stops faulting (this script's inputs):

| KV pages (rows) | KV bytes | faults at slack | clean at slack |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (64) | 36,864 | 61,440 | 65,536 |
| 2 (128) | 73,728 | 49,152 | 57,344 |
| 3 (192) | 110,592 | 16,384 | 32,768 |
| 4 (256) | 147,456 | — | 0 |

i.e. the kernel touches roughly the first ~170–250 rows' worth of bytes from the start of the cache regardless of its size. We saw the

items.title: [RFC] Rerun code skips in rerun-disabled-tests
items.author: amdfaa
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

`rerun-disabled-tests` (`PYTORCH_TEST_RERUN_DISABLED_TESTS=1`) reruns tests that are still skipped by a DISABLED GitHub issue, so a run of greens can justify closing that issue. This RFC adds the same kind of signal for a code skip: a skip for a known failure on a machine that can run the test. A capability skip stays skipped. That is a missing library, `onlyCUDA`, `skipIf` / `skipUnless`, `requires_*`, or a version floor.

Two drafts start this work:

- PyTorch, which publishes the signal and does not delete decorators: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/199916
- test-infra, which would later open one daily draft proposing deletions and does not merge them: https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/9026

## Motivation

| Who | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Test authors | A skip for a known failure can outlive the failure. With no GitHub issue to close, nothing prompts deleting the decorator. |
| CI | The nightly job already reruns DISABLED-issue skips. A code skip never produces a pass or a fail. |

## Background

A DISABLED issue skip already has a loop. While the issue is open, the nightly job runs the test. 150 greens in 7 days and 0 reds, plus 14 quiet days, are the bar for closing the issue. Closing it removes the skip.

A code skip has no issue. The decorator is the only record, and it stays in force during `rerun-disabled-tests`. The nightly job cannot tell a fixed code skip from one that still fails.

This RFC leaves the issue path and the `rerun_disabled_tests` upload unchanged. Code-skip reruns go to a separate prefix, `rerun_disabled_code_skips`.

```
Python skip decorator
        ↓
mark safe-to-rerun skips
        ↓
pytest collection temporarily removes those skips
        ↓
test body passes, fails, or remains skipped
        ↓
JUnit XML retains the original skip reason
        ↓
results upload to rerun_disabled_code_skips
        ↓
test-infra can eventually propose deleting fixed decorators
```

Only code skips are marked safe to rerun. Capability skips are not marked.

Collection drops those marks for that job only. The decorator stays in the source file.

The body then passes, fails, or remains skipped. It remains skipped when a capability skip still applies. A pass or a fail does not edit the file.

The JUnit row keeps the original skip reason, so a pass or a fail can still be matched to the decorator that was lifted.

Those rows upload to `rerun_disabled_code_skips` and are not added to `rerun_disabled_tests`.

test-infra can later propose deleting decorators that clear the same bar as closing a DISABLED issue: 150 greens in 7 days and 0 reds. There is no 14-day quiet period, because a code skip has no issue. https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/9026 is that last step. It would open one daily draft pull request. That draft does not merge.

## Goals

- Run code skips in `rerun-disabled-tests`.
- Leave capability skips skipped, on every platform.
- Keep the original skip reason on the result when the body passes or fails.
- Upload code-skip reruns only to `rerun_disabled_code_skips`.
- Leave `rerun_disabled_tests` unchanged.
- Propose decorator deletions in a later human-reviewed draft. Do not delete them here.

## Non-goals

- Deleting decorators in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/199916.
- Merging a deletion from https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/9026.
- Rerunning capability skips.
- Changing the DISABLED-issue path, its upload, or its 14 quiet days.
- Limiting the split to one platform.

## Alternatives

- Leave code skips until someone deletes them by hand. A fixed test stays skipped, with no green-run count behind a deletion.
- Upload code-skip reruns into `rerun_disabled_tests`. This RFC uses a separate prefix so the existing collection stays as it is.
- Rerun every skip. Failures on a machine that cannot run the test would be mixed in with real regressions.

## Additional context

- PyTorch: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/199916
- test-infra: https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/9026
- Deletion bar: 150 greens in 7 days and 0 reds. No 14-day quiet period.

items.title: [Inductor] _dump_launch_params races under pytest-xdist
items.author: kevint324
items.body_excerpt:
## Describe the bug

`test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py` can fail intermittently when it is run with pytest-xdist. The `_dump_launch_params` helper derives one shared path from `sys.argv[0]`. In the CI invocation below, every worker sees `sys.argv[0] == "-c"`, so all workers use the same `-c.launch_params` file.

The helper checks `os.path.exists()` and then calls `os.remove()`. Another worker can remove the file between those two operations, causing a `FileNotFoundError` before the test body starts. The same race can occur in the cleanup in `finally`.

The failure is in the upstream test helper and does not depend on the computation performed by the test. The failure is intermittent because it depends on worker scheduling.

The relevant test was:

```text
KernelTests::test_triton_kernel_2d_autotune_grad_False_dynamic_True_backend_inductor_grid_type_2_tdlp_1
```

The current helper on PyTorch `main` still uses the shared path:

```python
launch_params_file = f"{os.path.abspath(sys.argv[0])}.launch_params"
if value == "1" and os.path.exists(launch_params_file):
    os.remove(launch_params_file)
```

## Error logs

The failing command was:

```bash
coverage run -m pytest -p no:faulthandler \
  pytorch/test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py \
  -v -n 8 --timeout=720 --disable-warnings
```

Observed traceback:

```text
File ".../test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py", line 1336, in test_triton_kernel_2d_autotune
    with _dump_launch_params(tdlp):
File "/usr/lib/python3.12/contextlib.py", line 137, in __enter__
    return next(self.gen)
File ".../test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py", line 73, in _dump_launch_params
    os.remove(launch_params_file)
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../test/inductor/-c.launch_params'
```

The module result was:

```text
1 failed, 333 passed, 103 skipped
```

## Versions

- PyTorch source revision: `6f49d1f0287c449c186339782878346ad34847bd`
- PyTorch `main` checked on 2026-10-15: `64f6a5984749fc382465a3713ddd180bd60484e1`
- Python: 3.12.3
- pytest: 7.4.3
- pytest-xdist: 3.8.0
- Triton: 3.4.0

The source-level race can occur whenever multiple workers share the same launch-params path, while whether it manifests depends on worker scheduling.

## Proposed fix

Use a launch-params path unique to each xdist worker/process, and make the producer and cleanup code use that same path. Merely ignoring `FileNotFoundError` would hide the exception but would still allow workers to delete one another's files.

A possible implementation is to add the xdist worker name only when pytest-xdist is active, preserving the existing filename for serial runs:

```python
def _launch_params_file():
    path = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[0])
    worker = os.environ.get("PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER")
    if worker:
        path = f"{path}.{worker}"
    return f"{path}.launch_params"
```

The launch-params writer and `_dump_launch_params` cleanup should both use this helper.

items.title: [Serve][LLM] Preserve request-router callbacks for reserving out-of-band replica picks
items.author: eicherseiji
items.body_excerpt:
## Problem

The application-router scale-from-zero fallback in `RouterApplication._choose_replica` uses two selection modes:

1. It first calls `handle.choose_replica(..., _reserve=False)`.
2. If that pick times out, it falls back to the normal reserving `handle.choose_replica(...)`.

The pick-only path calls `RequestRouter.on_request_routed(..., result=None)`, as added in #66489. The reserving path normally calls `on_request_routed` during `handle.dispatch()`.

For the application router, HAProxy performs the actual dispatch, so `handle.dispatch()` is never called. A selection that succeeds through the reserving fallback therefore never invokes `on_request_routed`.

This can leave stateful request-router bookkeeping inconsistent. For example:

- `CapacityQueueRouter` can leave its token in `_pending_tokens`.
- Prefix-aware routing does not record the selected replica for the request.

The normal `_reserve=False` path is not affected.

## Current control flow

The relevant code in #66519 is equivalent to:

```python
async def pick(**kwargs) -> str:
    async with handle.choose_replica(*route_args, **kwargs) as selection:
        # Return to HAProxy; handle.dispatch() is intentionally not called.
        return selection._replica.replica_id.to_full_id_str()

try:
    # This path calls on_request_routed(..., result=None).
    return await asyncio.wait_for(
        pick(_reserve=False), timeout=PICK_ONLY_TIMEOUT_S
    )
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    # This path reserves a slot but never calls on_request_routed because
    # HAProxy, rather than DeploymentHandle.dispatch(), sends the request.
    return await pick()
```

The two paths currently have different callback behavior:

```text
choose_replica(_reserve=False)
    -> select replica
    -> on_request_routed(..., None)
    -> return replica to HAProxy

choose_replica()  # fallback
    -> select and reserve replica
    -> return replica to HAProxy
    -> exit context and release reservation
    -> no handle.dispatch()
    -> no on_request_routed()
```

## Minimal reproducer / regression-test shape

This can be reproduced at the `AsyncioRouter` level with the existing `TestChooseReplica` fixture and its recording request router:

```python
@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_reserved_out_of_band_pick_reports_routing_decision(setup_router):
    router, request_router = setup_router
    replica = install_one_fake_replica(request_router)
    payload = {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}

    # This is the application-router fallback: choose a reserving selection,
    # return its identity to an external dispatcher, and never call dispatch().
    async with router.choose_replica(dummy_request_metadata(), payload) as selection:
        assert selection._replica is replica

    # Current behavior: []
    # Desired out-of-band behavior: one (payload, replica ID, None) callback.
    assert len(request_router.routed_requests) == 1
    pending_request, replica_id, result = request_router.routed_requests[0]
    assert pending_request.args == [payload]
    assert replica_id == replica.replica_id
    assert result is None
```

For comparison, changing the selection to `_reserve=False` makes the assertion pass today because #66489 added the callback to that path:

```python
async with router.choose_replica(
    dummy_request_metadata(), payload, _reserve=False
) as selection:
    pass

assert len(request_router.routed_requests) == 1
```

A `CapacityQueueRouter`-focused regression test can additionally assert that the request ID does not remain in `_pending_tokens` after the out-of-band decision is reported and later completed or cancelled.

## Desired behavior

Support an explicit out-of-band dispatch lifecycle for reserving selections. When an application router reserves a replica only to make a routing decision for HAProxy, Serve should:

- preserve the scale-from-zero/autoscaling behavior of a reserving selection;
- call `on_request_routed(pending_request, replica_id, None)` exactly once after selection;
- release the temporary replica reservation safely when the context exits;
- clean up state correctly if the selection is cancelled or times out.

This could be modeled as an internal `choose_replica` option for out-of-band dispatch rather than having the application router call request-router internals directly, for example:

```python
async with handle.choose_replica(
    *route_args,
    _reserve=True,
    _out_of_band_dispatch=True,
    _timeout_s=remaining_decision_time,
) as selection:
    return selection._replica.replica_id.to_full_id_str()
```

The exact API is open to discussion; the important part is that selection, timeout/cancellation, callback delivery, and reservation cleanup are owned by the router loop as one lifecycle.

## Context

Found while reviewing #66519. The relevant fallback is in `python/ray/llm/_internal/serve/core/ingress/router_application.py`.

items.title: [RFC]: Support Encode/Prefill/Decode (EPD) Disaggregation in AIBrix Gateway
items.author: varungup90
items.body_excerpt: ### Summary This RFC proposes adding Encode/Prefill/Decode (EPD) disaggregation support to AIBrix Gateway. Today, AIBrix supports Prefill/Decode (PD) disaggregation. With growing multimodal workloads, the encoding stage can also become a significant and independently scalable part of inference. EPD disaggregation separates inference into three stages: * Encode (E): Process multimodal inputs such as image, video, or audio and generate intermediate representations. * Prefill (P): Process prompt tokens and encoder outputs and generate KV cache. * Decode (D): Perform autoregressive token generation. The Gateway should become aware of these worker roles and route requests to the appropriate Encode, Prefill, and Decode worker pools. ### Motivation Encode, Prefill, and Decode have different compute and memory characteristics. Running all stages on the same workers can lead to resource contention and makes it difficult to scale each stage independently. EPD disaggregation enables: * Independent scaling of Encode, Prefill, and Decode workers. * Better resource utilization for multimodal workloads. * Different hardware or parallelism configurations for each stage. * Isolation of expensive multimodal encoding from Prefill/Decode workloads. * Reuse of the existing AIBrix PD routing architecture for multimodal serving. vLLM has started supporting disaggregated encoder architectures, including EPD-style deployments: * https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/user_guide/feature_guide/epd_disaggregation.html * https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/disagg_encoder/ ### Proposed Change Extend AIBrix Gateway’s existing PD disaggregation support to understand an additional Encode worker role. Conceptually: For multimodal requests, the Gateway should: 1. Identify compatible Encode, Prefill, and Decode workers. 2. Select workers using the existing AIBrix load-balancing framework. 3. Pass the required routing/transfer metadata to the inference engine. 4. Allow the inference engine and its connectors to handle encoder-output and KV-cache transfers. For text-only requests, the Encode stage can be bypassed and existing PD routing can continue to be used. The implementation should reuse the existing PD routing infrastructure as much as possible rather than introducing a separate routing architecture. Initial Scope * Add encode as a supported worker role alongside prefill and decode. * Discover and maintain Encode/Prefill/Decode worker pools. * Extend PD routing to select a compatible E/P/D execution path. * Support multimodal requests requiring an Encode stage. * Keep encoder-output and KV-cache transfer outside of the Gateway. * Add basic stage-level routing metrics and failure handling. Future work can explore encoder-cache-aware routing, heterogeneous hardware selection, and independent autoscaling of E/P/D worker pools. Open Questions * Should Encode workers be shared across multiple Prefill/Decode pools? * What metadata should the Gateway provide to coordinate encoder-output transfer? * Should worker selection happen in E → P → D order, or should Decode/Prefill capacity drive the selection first? * How much of the existing PD router can be generalized into an EPD stage-aware router? ### Alternatives Considered _No response_ ### Area Not sure

items.title: [Bug] /v1/messages/count_tokens returns 501 through the gateway
items.author: theminjunchoi
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` can't be used through the gateway. vLLM and SGLang both serve it next to `/v1/messages`, and it's what the Anthropic SDK calls for `client.messages.count_tokens()`.

The request does reach the gateway plugin, because it matches the `/v1/messages` PathPrefix on both the reserved route and the per-model routes. But `validateRequestBody` matches paths exactly and has no case for it, so the plugin answers `501 unknown request path`.

Adding the case alone isn't enough. The response is just `{"input_tokens": N}`, with no `model` or `usage`, so `processLanguageResponse` treats it as an unknown response and replaces it with a 500. `/tokenize` ran into the same thing and is excluded in `isLanguageRequest` for that reason (#2732).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy a vLLM model behind the gateway.
2. Send `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` with `{"model": "<model>", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}`.
3. The gateway returns 501 `unknown request path`.

I hit both the 501 and the 500 in unit tests against main (9190b145). I haven't run it on a live cluster.

### Expected behavior

The request is routed by `model` like `/v1/messages`, and the engine's response is passed back unchanged. There's nothing to meter, since the endpoint only counts tokens.

### Environment

- AIBrix version: main (9190b145)
- LLM(s) being used: vLLM, SGLang

Area: Gateway

items.title: [Bug] ModelRouter never updates an existing HTTPRoute
items.author: theminjunchoi
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

ModelRouter creates a model's HTTPRoute once and never touches it again. `createHTTPRoute` ignores `AlreadyExists`, and the resync added in #2873 only recreates routes that are missing.

This bites on a default install. With no routing strategy set, the plugin just adds the `model` header and Envoy sends the request through that model's HTTPRoute, so the paths the route was created with are the only ones that work.

It shows up in two ways:

- After an upgrade, models that were already deployed don't get the paths added since v0.7.0 (`/tokenize`, `/pooling`, `/v1/score` and so on). Those requests 404 until someone deletes the route and lets it get recreated.
- Changing the port label, the service-name annotation or `model-router-custom-paths` on a running workload has no effect. `updateRouteFromWorkload` sees the change, but it only calls `createHTTPRoute`, which hits `AlreadyExists`. A new `AIBRIX_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` never gets applied either.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy a model on v0.7.0 with no routing strategy.
2. Upgrade to main.
3. `POST /tokenize` for that model returns 404, and `<model>-router` still has the old paths.

I reproduced this and the port change in unit tests and with envtest on main (c60f1d91). I haven't tried the actual upgrade on a cluster.

### Expected behavior

The resync should also update an existing route when it's out of date, not just recreate missing ones.

### Environment

- AIBrix version: main (c60f1d91), default install

Area: Gateway

for a user with a tpm limit, `validateRequestBody` rejects a streamed chat completion that does not set `stream_options.include_usage`, because without it the engine sends no usage chunk and there is nothing to meter. the check is tied to `requestPath == PathChatCompletions` (`pkg/plugins/gateway/util.go`), so the same request on `/v1/completions` is accepted. the engine then streams no usage, `processStreamingResponse` ends with a zero total, and `HandleResponseBody` skips the tpm increment

measured on main @ d0500b0, user with `Tpm: 1000`:

| request | accepted | tokens metered |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions`, `stream: true`, no `stream_options` | no, 400 `include usage for stream options not set` | n/a |
| `/v1/chat/completions`, `stream: true`, `include_usage: true` | yes | from the usage chunk |
| `/v1/completions`, `stream: true`, no `stream_options` | **yes** | **0** |
| `/v1/completions`, `stream: true`, `include_usage: true` | yes | from the usage chunk |

so a tpm limited user who streams legacy completions without `stream_options` is never counted. rpm is still enforced

### Steps to Reproduce

drop this in `pkg/plugins/gateway/` and run `go test ./pkg/plugins/gateway -run TestStreamedCompletionsWithoutIncludeUsage -v`

```go
package gateway

import (
	"fmt"
	"testing"

	"github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/pkg/utils"
)

func TestStreamedCompletionsWithoutIncludeUsage(t *testing.T) {
	user := utils.User{Name: "u", Rpm: 10, Tpm: 1000}
	reqs := []struct{ name, path, body string }{
		{"chat, no stream_options", PathChatCompletions, `{"model":"m","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}`},
		{"chat, include_usage", PathChatCompletions, `{"model":"m","stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}`},
		{"completions, no stream_options", PathCompletions, `{"model":"m","stream":true,"prompt":"hi"}`},
		{"completions, include_usage", PathCompletions, `{"model":"m","stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true},"prompt":"hi"}`},
	}
	for _, r := range reqs {
		_, _, _, stream, errRes := validateRequestBody("r", r.path, []byte(r.body), user)
		fmt.Printf("%-32s stream=%v rejected=%v\n", r.name, stream, errRes != nil)
	}
	noUsage := "data: {\"id\":\"cmpl-1\",\"choices\":[{\"text\":\"hello\",\"finish_reason\":\"stop\"}]}\n\ndata: [DONE]\n\n"
	usage, _ := processStreamingResponse("r1", []byte(noUsage), true)
	fmt.Printf("completions stream, no usage chunk    total=%d\n", usage.TotalTokens)
	withUsage := "data: {\"id\":\"cmpl-1\",\"choices\":[{\"text\":\"hello\",\"finish_reason\":\"stop\"}]}\n\ndata: {\"id\":\"cmpl-1\",\"choices\":[],\"usage\":{\"prompt_tokens\":2,\"completion_tokens\":1,\"total_tokens\":3}}\n\ndata: [DONE]\n\n"
	usage, _ = processStreamingResponse("r2", []byte(withUsage), true)
	fmt.Printf("completions stream, with usage chunk  total=%d\n", usage.TotalTokens)
}
```

output

```
chat, no stream_options          stream=true rejected=true
chat, include_usage              stream=true rejected=false
completions, no stream_options   stream=true rejected=false
completions, include_usage       stream=true rejected=false
completions stream, no usage chunk    total=0
completions stream, with usage chunk  total=3
```

### Expected behavior

`/v1/completions` gets the same treatment as chat for a tpm limited user. two ways, your call: reject with the same 400 when `stream_options.include_usage` is missing, or set it on the way to the engine so the client does not have to. the first is a few lines in `validateCompletionRequest`, the second changes the body and needs the content length update

### Environment

- AIBrix version: main @ d0500b0
- Deployment environment: none, unit level reproduction with `go test`
- Cloud provider: n/a
- LLM(s) being used: n/a, the no usage stream shape is what an openai compatible engine sends when `include_usage` is not set, not captured from a live vllm here
- Client library version: n/a

### Area

Gateway

found with ai assistance, i reran the reproduction myself on current main. i sent this together with the `/v1/messages` case to maintainers@aibrix.ai on the 11th, opening it here now that #3008 covered the other half in public

items.title: [Bug] Evicting one branch of the Preble prefix tree drops pods from its parent prefix
items.author: hmdsefi
items.body_excerpt:
## 🐛 Describe the bug

`LPRadixCache.evictNode` in `pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer/tree.go` removes the evicted node's pods from every parent node. It does not check whether another child of that parent still has the pod.

prefix-cache-preble records the target pod on every node of the request's path (`PostRouteUpdate`), so a parent prefix lists every pod that cached any of its branches. When one branch expires, the parent and the root lose those pods, even if another branch on the same pod is still cached. Requests that share the parent prefix then no longer match that pod, and the router falls back to cost-based routing.

## Steps to Reproduce

Unit level, with `NewLPRadixCache(2)`:

1. `AddPrefix([1 2 3], "m1", "default/p1")`, `AddPrefix([1 2 4], "m1", "default/p1")` and `AddPrefix([1 2 4], "m1", "default/p2")`. The tree is `[1 2]` with the children `[3]` and `[4]`.
2. Make only the `[4]` node older than the 5 minute TTL and call `Evict(time.Now())`.
3. Call `MatchPrefix([1 2 9], "m1", [p1, p2])`.

At d0500b03 it returns the matched tokens `[1 2]` and no pods.

## Expected behavior

`[1 2]` should still match p1, which still caches `[1 2 3]`. p2 only had `[1 2]` through the evicted branch, so it is right to drop p2.

## Environment

- AIBrix version: main at d0500b03
- Deployment environment: unit test of pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer
- Cloud provider (if applicable): n/a
- LLM(s) being used: not model specific
- Client library version (if applicable): n/a

## Area

Gateway

I'd like to fix this. I have a change with tests ready and will open a PR.

items.title: [Bug] A recovered Batch job past its window with no execution metadata never finishes expiring
items.author: Jackmeson1
items.body_excerpt:
## 🐛 Describe the bug

An in-progress Batch job that is already past its completion window when the metadata service recovers it, and that has no execution metadata (`status.execution is None`), never finishes expiring. It stays `in_progress` with the `expired` condition set, and clients keep seeing `in_progress`.

On recovery, `job_committed_handler` (`python/aibrix/aibrix/batch/batch_manager.py:554` at `99325e7`) does not schedule overdue work and calls `expire_job` instead. For an in-progress job, `expire_job` (line 1184) persists the expired condition and leaves finalization to the live driver it then signals. A recovered job has no driver. The orphan cleanup path that would finish it runs only when `job_expired.status.execution is not None` (line 1258). Every later expiry pass from the scheduler then returns early, because the job is already `IN_PROGRESS` with `EXPIRED` (line 1215). Nothing else owns the job, so it never becomes terminal.

The same recovery with `execution = {}` (not `None`) does finish `expired`, and an overdue `created` job finalizes `expired` as expected (`batch-api.rst:147` documents expiry after the window).

## Steps to Reproduce

From `python/aibrix` at `99325e7`, put this in `tests/batch/` and run it with `pytest`:

<details><summary>test_overdue_recovery.py</summary>

```python
import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

os.environ.setdefault("SECRET_KEY", "test-secret-key-for-testing")

from aibrix.batch.batch_manager import BatchManager
from aibrix.batch.job_entity import (
    BatchJob,
    BatchJobEndpoint,
    BatchJobSpec,
    BatchJobState,
    BatchJobStatus,
    CompletionWindow,
    ConditionType,
    ObjectMeta,
    TypeMeta,
)
from aibrix.context import InfrastructureContext
from aibrix.metadata.api.v1.batch import _batch_job_to_openai_response


class _Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        self.appended = []

    def append_job(self, job_id):
        self.appended.append(job_id)


def _overdue_in_progress_job(job_id, execution):
    created = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=25)
    job = BatchJob(
        typeMeta=TypeMeta(apiVersion="batch/v1", kind="Job"),
        metadata=ObjectMeta(
            name=f"job-{job_id}", namespace="default", uid=f"uid-{job_id}",
            creationTimestamp=created, resourceVersion=None, deletionTimestamp=None,
        ),
        spec=BatchJobSpec(
            input_file_id=f"input-{job_id}",
            endpoint=BatchJobEndpoint.CHAT_COMPLETIONS.value,
            completion_window=CompletionWindow.TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS.expires_at(),
        ),
        status=BatchJobStatus(
            jobID=job_id, state=BatchJobState.IN_PROGRESS,
            createdAt=created, inProgressAt=created,
        ),
    )
    job.status.request_counts.total = 1
    job.status.execution = execution
    return job


@pytest.mark.asyncio
@pytest.mark.parametrize("execution", [None, {}], ids=["execution-none", "execution-empty"])
async def test_recovered_overdue_in_progress_job_expires(execution):
    manager = BatchManager(InfrastructureContext())
    scheduler = _Scheduler()
    manager.set_scheduler(scheduler)
    job = _overdue_in_progress_job(f"overdue-{execution is None}", execution)

    await manager.job_committed_handler(job)  # recovery after a restart
    await manager.expire_job(job.job_id)  # the scheduler's next expiry pass

    assert scheduler.appended == []  # overdue work is not scheduled
    current = manager._done_jobs.get(job.job_id) or await manager.get_job(job.job_id)
    assert current.status.state == BatchJobState.FINALIZED, (
        f"state={current.status.state.value} condition={current.status.condition} "
        f"client={_batch_job_to_openai_response(current).status}"
    )
    assert current.status.condition == ConditionType.EXPIRED
    assert _batch_job_to_openai_response(current).status == "expired"
```

</details>

`execution-empty` passes. `execution-none` fails with:

```text
AssertionError: state=in_progress condition=expired client=in_progress
```

The test calls the recovery handler and one more expiry pass directly; it does not restart a process against durable storage.

## Expected behavior

A recovered job past its window finishes `expired` (state `finalized`, condition `expired`, client status `expired`), the same as when it has an empty execution record or was still `created`.

## Environment

- AIBrix version: `main` at `99325e7`
- Deployment environment: Batch API, metadata service recovery; reproduced in-process on Linux, Python 3.10.12
- LLM(s) being used: none

## Area

Batch

I don't plan to send a fix for this soon, so anyone is welcome to take it. A fix probably belongs in `expire_job`: route a recovered job that has no live driver and no execution reference through the existing stopped-job finalization, without stamping `FINALIZED` directly and so bypassing output finalization.

This report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); the test above was run against `main`.

items.title: [Bug] KPA panic mode never holds replicas and reports idle workloads as panic
items.author: AarnavNoble
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

KPA's panic mode doesn't behave as its code describes, and part of that code can never run. Before sending a fix I'd like to agree on which behavior is wanted, since there are two reasonable directions (below).

**1. The "no scale-down while in panic" rule is dead code.** `computeTargetReplicas` (`pkg/controller/podautoscaler/algorithm/kpa.go`) keeps the highest pod count seen during panic in `maxPanicPods` and refuses to go below it:

```go
// We do not scale down while in panic mode. Only increases will be applied.
if desiredPodCount > maxPanicPods { ... context.SetMaxPanicPods(maxPanicPods) }
desiredPodCount = maxPanicPods
```

But the context the controller passes in is `baseScalingContext`, where `GetMaxPanicPods()` returns `0` and `SetMaxPanicPods` is a no-op (`pkg/controller/podautoscaler/context/context.go`). The controller also builds a new context on every reconcile, so `InPanicMode` doesn't carry over either. Each reconcile therefore just takes `max(stable, panic)` for that reconcile, and the panic-mode recommendation can go down while still in panic. The unit tests use `mockScalingContext`, which does store `MaxPanicPods`, so they pass while production never gets this behavior.

**2. An idle workload is reported as panic.** `shouldEnterPanicMode` returns `true` whenever `StableValue <= 0`, so zero traffic (stable 0, panic 0) produces the reason `"panic mode scaling"` and the `Operating in panic mode.` log line.

**3. Panic entry doesn't use Knative's rule.** Panic is entered when `panic / stable > panicThreshold`. Knative enters panic when the panic-window pod count is at least `panicThreshold` times the ready pods (`dppc / readyPods >= panicThreshold`) and stays in it until a full stable window has passed without that. The code computes `isOverPanicThreshold` with Knative's rule but only logs it.

In practice the default 5-minute scale-down cooldown (`stabilizeRecommendation`) hides most of point 1, since it keeps the highest recommendation of the last 5 minutes anyway. With a shorter `scale-down-cooldown-window`, nothing holds replicas during a burst.

### Steps to Reproduce

Calling `KPAAlgorithm.ComputeRecommendation` the way the controller does (a fresh `NewBaseScalingContext()` per call, one `POD` metric `concurrency` with `targetValue: "10"`, default annotations):

| Call | Current pods | Stable value | Panic value | Desired | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 10 | 25 | 8 | panic mode scaling |
| 2 | 8 | 3 | 6.5 | 6 | panic mode scaling |
| 3 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 2 | panic mode scaling |

Call 2 is still in panic (6.5 / 3 > 2) but recommends fewer pods than call 1, and `GetMaxPanicPods()` is still `0` after both calls. Call 3 has no traffic and is labeled panic.

### Expected behavior

- No `panic` label (reason, log, metrics) when there is no traffic.
- One of these for panic hold, which is what I'd like your input on:
  - **A. Implement it.** Keep panic state per PodAutoscaler across reconciles (the reconciler already keeps per-PodAutoscaler state, such as the recommendation history in `stabilizeRecommendation`, and releases it on delete), enter panic with Knative's `dppc / readyPods >= panicThreshold`, and hold the peak until a stable window passes without panic.
  - **B. Remove it.** Drop `maxPanicPods`, `GetMaxPanicPods`/`SetMaxPanicPods` and the hold logic, document that KPA scales on `max(stable, panic)` while panicking, and leave holding replicas to the scale-down cooldown.

A is closer to Knative and to KPA's docs. B is smaller and keeps one mechanism for holding replicas. I'm happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer, along with the idle-panic fix.

### Environment

- AIBrix version: `main` at 177ba311
- Deployment environment: unit-level reproduction against the KPA algorithm and the real `baseScalingContext`

### Area

Orchestration (controllers, CRDs)

items.title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash thinking output degenerates into repeated '!' under multi-tool agentic prompts
items.author: ech0potato
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

When serving zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (native FP8 checkpoint) with SGLang, requests with a complex system prompt + multiple tools + `tool_choice=auto` cause the model's reasoning/thinking output to degenerate into an endless stream of `!` characters. Simple requests work correctly.

## Environment

- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash`
- SGLang: `0.0.0.dev1+gd6ab04bdf1`
- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA H20 (Hopper sm90), TP=8, EP=8
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (native FP8)

Launch args:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model \
  --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47
```

## Repro

Simple request (works fine):

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "model": "/model",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "1+1=? answer with a number only"}],
    "max_tokens": 100
  }'
# -> content "2", reasoning content is normal
```

Complex request (degenerates):

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "model": "/model",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a coding agent. Be concise. Use tools when needed. You have bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep tools available... (long agentic system prompt ~2000 tokens)"},
      {"role": "user", "content": "1+1=? answer with a number only"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 200,
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "tools": [
      {"type":"function","function":{"name":"bash","description":"run shell","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"command":{"type":"string"}},"required":["command"]}}},
      {"type":"function","function":{"name":"read","description":"read file","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}},"required":["path"]}}},
      {"type":"function","function":{"name":"write","description":"write file","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"},"content":{"type":"string"}},"required":["path","content"]}}}
    ]
  }'
```

## Observed behavior

The streaming response's `reasoning_content` field contains only `!` characters (hundreds of them, e.g. 1800+ `!` in a single response), and `content` is empty. The model never produces a real answer.

## What I've already tried

1. `--reasoning-parser glm45` -> degenerates (`reasoning_content` = `!!!!!`)
2. `--reasoning-parser deepseek-r1` -> degenerates (`reasoning_content` = `!!!!!`)
3. No reasoning-parser -> `<think>` block leaks into `content` (reasoning not stripped)
4. Disabling speculative decoding (MTP) entirely -> still degenerates (rules out MTP as the cause)
5. `chat_template_kwargs {"reasoning_effort": "low"}` -> still degenerates

## Notes / hypothesis

- GLM-5.3-Flash thinking is always-on (the chat template injects `<think>` unconditionally), controlled by `reasoning_effort` (low/high/max) rather than `enable_thinking`.
- Simple requests (short prompt, no tools, or a single simple tool) work correctly.
- The degeneration is triggered specifically by **complex system prompt + multiple tools + tool_choice=auto**.
- This may be related to how the reasoning parser interacts with tool-call parsing (`glm47`) for this model — the model appears to enter a repetition loop once it must reason about multiple tool definitions.
- Related: #36653 (MTP under TP>1) is a separate issue; this degeneration happens with MTP disabled too.

items.title: Add MXFP8 support for DeepEP-style MoE dispatch/combine kernels
items.author: dishamehra
items.body_excerpt:
The current DeepEP dispatch/combine paths used by vLLM are compatible with block-FP8 quantization, but do not yet support MXFP8. They would like to use MXFP8, specifically for decode nodes.

DeepEP currently has two dispatch/combine collective implementations for MoE models in vLLM:
- prefill / high_throughput: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_ht.py
- decode / low_latency: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_ll.py

Support ask:
- Add MXFP8 quantization format support to the dispatch/combine kernels
- Add support for a batched-format MXFP8 MoE kernel.
- Integrate the MXFP8 MoE kernel support into vLLM so that it is compatible with the low_latency DeepEP communication path.
 
The highest-priority path is: MXFP8 + decode / low_latency. It would also be useful to support: MXFP8 + prefill / high_throughput but low_latency decode support is the more important use case.

items.title: docs: track API, prose, HTML rendering, and broken-link findings
items.author: kangbintNV
items.body_excerpt:
## Scope

Documentation findings span API behavior, technical accuracy, prose, HTML rendering, and links. The examples below show one case for each issue type; all four identified broken links are listed. Source corrections are in PR #5494. After the docs are published, verify the rendered pages and link destinations.

## One example per issue type

- **API Contract (P0):** The [cascade API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/cascade.html) labels the `BatchPrefillWithSharedPrefixPagedKVCacheWrapper` constructor as `BatchDecodeWithSharedPrefixPagedKVCacheWrapper`.
- **Technical Accuracy (P1):** The [JAX FFI tutorial](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/tutorials/generated/jax_tvm_ffi/flashinfer_jax_tvm_ffi.html) says three additional packages are required but lists only two.
- **Grammar (P1):** The [attention API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/attention.html) says `for batch of requests`; it needs `for a batch of requests`.
- **Clarity (P1):** The [sampling API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/sampling.html) repeats `the sampling` in one sentence about deterministic sampling.
- **Punctuation (P1):** The [sampling API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/sampling.html) joins two independent sentences with a comma after `probabilities`.
- **Spelling (P1):** The [communication API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/comm.html) says `Initialization referece`.
- **Terminology (P2):** The [KV layout tutorial](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/tutorials/kv_layout.html) says `kV-Cache` instead of `KV-Cache`.
- **Formatting / HTML rendering (P0):** The [sampling API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/sampling.html) displays literal `:param logits:` and `:type logits:` inside the `sampling_from_logits` description instead of structured parameter fields.

## Broken Link (P0): all four cases

1. **CUDA Programmatic Dependent Launch, published API:** The [attention API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/attention.html) uses an [old URL](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/#programmatic-dependent-launch-and-synchronization) that returns 404. Use the [current CUDA section](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/programmatic-dependent-launch.html).
2. **FlashInfer MLA article, published API:** The [attention API](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/api/attention.html) links to a [missing article](http://flashinfer.ai/2025/02/10/flashinfer-deepseek-mla.html). Use the [FlashInfer 0.2 MLA section](https://flashinfer.ai/2024/12/16/flashinfer-v02-release.html#fused-multi-head-latent-attention-mla-decoding-kernel).
